executive_summary: Collection window February 29-March 6, 2028: Milan Fashion Week Fall/Winter 2028 women's shows, on the calendar confirmed in the 2028-02-28 report, took place within this window. Prada's own site published the house's runway lookbook for its Fall/Winter 2028 Milan show, and vogue.com independently reviewed the same show, both identifying an inverted-pleat cargo skirt -- a knee-length skirt built with box pleats sewn so the fold faces inward rather than outward, paired with structured cargo-style patch pockets, producing a flatter front panel than a conventional pleated skirt -- as a recurring construction across multiple looks. This is treated as genuine cross-sector corroboration, applying the identical reasoning already used for the 2028-01-24 Louis Vuitton, 2028-01-31 Dior, 2028-02-14 Proenza Schouler, 2028-02-21 Khaite, and 2028-02-28 Simone Rocha signals: one designer_origin source (the house's own lookbook) and one editorial source doing independent runway-review reporting, not a restatement of the house's own materials. Separately, FHCM (Federation de la Haute Couture et de la Mode), Paris Fashion Week's governing body, published its official calendar for Fall/Winter 2028 women's Paris Fashion Week this window, the final leg of the international fashion-month sequence following Milan's close, and wwd.com independently reported on the announcement with added confirmed-participant detail beyond a restatement of FHCM's own release -- the same fact pattern already applied to the 2028-02-28 CNMI/wwd.com Milan calendar-confirmation signal, the 2028-02-21 BFC/vogue.com London calendar-confirmation signal, the 2028-02-07 CFDA/wwd.com New York calendar-confirmation signal, and the 2028-01-10 FHCM/wwd.com Paris menswear calendar-confirmation signal. Per precedent 6 in the confidence-discipline precedents doc, these two signals' same-week co-occurrence is not treated as cross-sector corroboration between them; each is derived only from sources that address it directly. Paris's Fall/Winter 2028 women's shows themselves had not yet begun within this collection window (Feb 29-Mar 6) and, per the fashion-month sequencing established across this archive, are not expected to open until after this window closes; any runway coverage of Paris women's Fall/Winter 2028 shows is expected in a subsequent window, not retroactively folded into this one. The Khaite cantilevered-shoulder-blazer thread, the Proenza Schouler spiral-seam-wrap-coat thread, the Simone Rocha pearl-trimmed puff-sleeve dress thread, the resort 2028 puffer-shell skirt thread, the resale-demand signal on structured waist-tailoring, the obi-sash cocoon coat thread, and the opera-glove/'restraint dressing' thread all produced no new development this window and are not carried forward again absent fresh movement. The Margiela raw-edge thread remains closed out as of 2027-10-18. Met Gala 2027, Wales Bonner, and CFDA's Fashion Fund/Awards remain untracked going forward per standing convention.

top_signals.name: Prada Fall/Winter 2028 runway: inverted-pleat cargo skirt
top_signals.evidence: Prada published its own runway lookbook for its Fall/Winter 2028 show at Milan Fashion Week, and vogue.com independently reviewed the same show, both identifying a knee-length skirt built with box pleats sewn so the fold faces inward rather than outward, paired with structured cargo-style patch pockets -- producing a flatter front panel than a conventional pleated skirt -- repeated across multiple looks. The lookbook is the house's own first-party statement of the collection; vogue.com's review adds independent critical framing rather than restating the lookbook's own copy.
top_signals.index_note: Read as a single-runway-event silhouette observation at the designer-intent stage: a garment shown on one house's runway this window, not yet a claim of editorial trend consensus across other designers, retail buying, or social circulation.
top_signals.human_editor_note: derive_confidence() computes 'high' here (corroboration_count=2, two distinct sectors: designer_origin, editorial), and this report adopts that result rather than overriding it, applying the identical reasoning already used for the 2028-01-24 Louis Vuitton, 2028-01-31 Dior, 2028-02-14 Proenza Schouler, 2028-02-21 Khaite, and 2028-02-28 Simone Rocha signals: the second source is a genuinely distinct sector -- the house's own first-party lookbook (designer_origin) plus an independent editorial review, not two outlets in the same sector -- so the sector diversity is real, not a taxonomy artifact (precedent 3) or a mislabeled single underlying source (precedent 7). prada.com was already present in taxonomy.py's DOMAIN_SECTOR_MAP as designer_origin (no new domain-map entry required this run). confidence_source is set to 'derived' since the mechanical result is adopted as-is, no manual override.

top_signals.name: Paris confirms Fall/Winter 2028 women's Fashion Week dates
top_signals.evidence: FHCM, Paris Fashion Week's governing body, published its official calendar for Fall/Winter 2028 women's Paris Fashion Week this window, the final leg of the international fashion-month sequence following Milan's close. wwd.com independently reported on the announcement, adding a preliminary confirmed-designer-participant list not present in FHCM's own release -- this is treated as genuine independent second-sector reporting rather than a reprint of the primary announcement, the same distinction drawn for the 2028-02-28 mfw-fw28-womens-calendar-confirmed signal, the 2028-02-21 lfw-fw28-womens-calendar-confirmed signal, and the 2028-02-07 nyfw-fw28-womens-calendar-confirmed signal.
top_signals.index_note: Read as routine pre-season fashion-week logistics, not a style signal -- confirmation of a calendar date and participant list is not, itself, a garment, silhouette, or aesthetic claim.
top_signals.human_editor_note: derive_confidence() computes 'high' here (corroboration_count=2, two distinct sectors: institutional, editorial) and this report adopts that result rather than overriding it, applying the identical reasoning already used for the 2028-02-28 CNMI/wwd.com, 2028-02-21 BFC/vogue.com, 2028-02-07 CFDA/wwd.com, and 2028-01-10 FHCM/wwd.com calendar-confirmation signals: wwd.com's coverage adds confirmed-participant detail FHCM's own release did not include, which is genuine independent journalism, not a reprint of the primary announcement (contrast the 2027-09-06 fhcm.paris/laforma.club aggregator-reprint case under precedent 4). fhcm.paris was already present in taxonomy.py's DOMAIN_SECTOR_MAP as institutional (no new domain-map entry required this run). Per precedent 6, this signal's same-week co-occurrence with the Prada cargo-skirt signal is not treated as cross-sector corroboration between them -- each is derived only from sources addressing it directly. This signal announces the calendar for Paris's women's shows only; it is a separate announcement from the 2028-01-10 pfw-mens-fw28-calendar-confirmed signal (menswear) and is not treated as a continuation of that earlier signal_id. confidence_source is set to 'derived' rather than 'manual' since the mechanical result is adopted as-is.
